subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core framework-level plugin circuit breaker, and what default fail modes, storage model, and operator reset/status surfaces are acceptable for existing plugins?
rationale: Current code only has hook timeouts and plugin-local breakers; a shared breaker would add plugin API expectations, config/default behavior, runtime storage, status output, and operator controls that automation should not choose.

options.title: Design Core Breaker First
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-led design covering hook attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, and compatibility-safe default behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep Breakers Plugin-Owned
options.body: Defer a framework breaker and ask high-risk plugins to implement degradation through current hook/config surfaces.

options.title: Start Passive Telemetry Only
options.body: Implement hook timing and failure counters first, then decide active open/half-open quarantine behavior after deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design Core Breaker First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-led design covering hook attribution, SQLite-backed state, status/reset commands, and compatibility-safe default behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current-main hook runner, plugin status, and runtime state surfaces route most directly to Vincent Koc's recent merged work.
